hook: Don't let the premise talk you into skimming. The file sets up an absurd, almost cartoonish problem and then handles it with complete seriousness, and the payoff is a set of recorded phone messages near the end. Read those one at a time and notice how much changes between them.
whyItMatters: SCP-2875 belongs to the family of articles that take a silly concept and play it entirely straight, letting dry Foundation procedure do the comic work. Its tags include a prize-feature mark and an audio tag, and the voicemails are clearly built to be heard as well as read. It is also a compact lesson in how one addendum can recast the document above it.
thingsToNotice:
The voicemails tell a whole story from one side of a conversation. The caller slides from neighbourly small talk to worry to panic, while the phone number he keeps repeating turns into a grim running gag that survives to the very last message. The footnote is the real turn: it hints that the town's own officials may be tied to the origin of the problem, which makes the earliest calls read like a confession.

Also look at the rule about weapons. Because guns make things worse, the procedures force a slow, hands-on approach, and the task force lead's note speaks directly to anyone treating the whole thing as a joke.
